goal: Build Perfpal, a static-analysis tool that extracts performance-relevant heuristics from codebases, renders insightful visual bottleneck maps, and emits LLM-consumable quantifiable metrics to enable AI-driven optimization.
decisions: Project directory initialized at /home/ibrar/Perfpal.

A1: Product form = CLI only, outputs all artifacts to a directory.
A2: Target audience = local developers (not SaaS/CI-first).
B3: Visual output = static charts; form flexible, choose easiest to develop.
B4: Visual layer must expose architecture-level issues: dependency structure, component coupling, hot components — structural/architectural analysis, not just per-function metric heatmaps.
C5: C/C++ heuristics = include all sensible performance heuristics (founder: 'add them all if it isn't a huge issue').
C6: Python heuristics = same policy, include all sensible performance heuristics.

D8: LLM output = BOTH raw data (machine-readable) AND human-readable report.
D9: ONE target LLM only (no multi-LLM format variants).
E10: MVP = ONE language, heuristics only.
E11: No formal success criteria needed for now.
F12: License = source-available proprietary (free to use; modification and redistribution require explicit permission). CONSTRAINT: dependency choices must avoid copyleft (GPL-family) licenses.
G13: 'tp' = TypeScript confirmed.
G14: Why C/C++/Python first = shared foundations + C has most extensive documentation. [ASSUMPTION: MVP language = C — flagged for confirmation]
CONFIRMED-1: MVP is strictly static analysis; architecture designed so runtime-profile ingestion bolts on later without rewrite.
CONFIRMED-2: MVP language = C.
CONFIRMED-3: Heuristic scope = prioritized catalog for founder sign-off (NOT literally every heuristic).
CONFIRMED-4: Target LLM = undecided / keep generic. Design LLM-agnostic JSON schema; no vendor-specific tuning.
CONFIRMED-5: Output layout = 'perfpal-report/' default containing metrics.json, report.md, charts/.
open_risks: Language parsing for C must be robust; choosing between libclang, tree-sitter, or hybrid is the highest-priority architectural decision.
License constraint (no copyleft) limits dependency pool; must audit all transitive deps.
Architecture-level visualization for C (dependency structure, component coupling) requires call-graph/module-graph extraction — non-trivial due to headers/preprocessor.
Static analysis heuristics are approximate, not ground truth; must frame outputs as 'optimization candidates' to avoid LLM over-optimization on noisy signals.
No formal success criteria = harder to define 'done' for MVP; relying on acceptance criteria in spec instead.
